outcomes: Application code emits one structured record to one or more interchangeable sinks
Request and event boundaries accumulate context fields without sharing mutable logger state
Trace and structured-error metadata remain machine-readable in JSON output
A panicking logged value cannot unwind the application call that attempted to log it
nonGoals: Shipping, retaining, or querying logs in a remote service
Guaranteeing that arbitrary caller-owned objects are safe to marshal
Promising cross-runtime parity beyond the cases covered by the logging conformance corpus

requirements.text: Each sink write is panic-isolated so marshaling or formatting a hostile value cannot crash the logging caller.
Context-aware records apply field precedence in the order logger context, request FieldBag, call-site attributes, then framework-reserved fields.
Logger Flush and Close invoke every configured sink and return the first sink error they observe.
Every emitted record carries level, message, timestamp, logger name, attributes, optional context, optional trace identity, and optional structured error information.
